title: skills get --full puts SKILL.md first only by lexicographic luck
body:
`skills get --full` prints skills.Paths(name) in order and writes the "--- <path> ---" separator only for i > 0, so the contract u2g states — SKILL.md, then every references file under a header naming its path — holds only because skills.Paths sorts lexicographically and 'S' (0x53) sorts before 'r' (0x72). A top-level file added to the bundle that sorts before SKILL.md (README.md, CHANGELOG.md, AGENTS.md) would be printed FIRST and, being index 0, with no header at all — silently inverting the documented order and leaving the reader no way to tell where one file ends and the next begins. Leading with SKILL.md explicitly, or giving every file its header, makes the contract true by construction.
evidence: internal/cli/skills.go:185-190 (the `if i > 0` separator) with internal/skills/skills.go:111 (sort.Strings); TestSkillsGetFullPrintsEveryFile asserts strings.HasPrefix(out, SKILL.md) and so encodes the same accident
